clue.text: One composer and another shortly visiting down under

indicators.note: shortly asks for the name cut short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: another composer: Irving Berlin, the American songwriter
Oz is the informal name for Australia, down under; the trimmed name visits it by standing beside it

explanation.surface: Two composers seem to be on an Australian tour together.
explanation.walkthrough: Irving Berlin loses his last letter and is joined by OZ to give BERLIOZ, the French composer of the Symphonie fantastique.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a French Romantic composer, so he is one composer among many.

clue.text: In life, king's vigour

indicators.note: in places the royal letter inside the word for life

parts.note: bio, short for biography, is a life story
R, for Rex, is the standard abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch shows energy throughout his life.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is liveliness and spirit, an Italian loan word meaning energetic verve.

clue.text: Not happy about one having to mount platform

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for unhappy is read backwards
to mount is to get up on and into, so the single letter climbs inside the turned word

parts.note: sad is the opposite of happy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant is made to step up onto a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall, for speakers or a high table.

clue.text: Mayfly makes border in record time

indicators.note: in places the edging word inside the abbreviation for a short record

parts.note: an EP, extended play, is a short record
an era is a period of time
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A short-lived insect crosses a border in record-breaking time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera is the scientific genus of the mayfly, an insect whose adult life lasts about a day.

clue.text: A short whisky say at noon that dulls the pain

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'something that dulls the pain'

indicators.note: short tells us to cut the final letter from the drink category

parts.note: taken as written
whisky is an example of a spirit, hence 'say'
N is a standard abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A midday dram of whisky is offered as a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink in the surface is a red herring for the cure; the actual remedy is the common tablet ASPIRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common analgesic tablet taken to relieve headaches and other aches.

clue.text: Sport, an energy-filled fight

indicators.note: a fight filled with something holds it inside

parts.note: a war is a large-scale fight
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sporting contest turns into a lively brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like games, but here it is the verb meaning to have on, as in sporting a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport a garment is to wear it, especially to show it off.

clue.text: Jam pot's first in hamper

parts.note: to jam things in is to cram them

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the vessel word

parts.note: the opening letter of pot

explanation.surface: A jar of jam is packed into a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket, but here it is the verb meaning to restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp someone is to restrict or hinder them, as in cramping their style.

clue.text: Taking afternoon off, make for island

indicators.note: taking the letter off means removing it from the verb that follows

parts.note: to create is to make
A is short for afternoon, as in p.m. or 'a' on timetables

explanation.surface: Someone takes the afternoon off work and heads for a holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest Greek island, in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Half a ball missing in match

indicators.note: half tells us to keep only the front half of the word
missing confirms that the rest of the word is gone, dropped entirely

parts.note: ball is slang for this body part

explanation.surface: A cricket or football match is held up because half the ball has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The front four letters of the eight-letter word are kept. A test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is an international match, especially in cricket or rugby, between national sides.

clue.text: Time to cut down forest for first book in series

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to hew a tree is to cut it down
the Forest of Arden in Warwickshire, setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: It is time to fell trees to begin a project.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition needs literary knowledge: Trollope's Barchester Chronicles open with this novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope's novel of 1855 is the opening volume of his Barchester Chronicles sequence.

clue.text: Postwar children pack large underclothes

indicators.note: to pack something is to stuff it inside, so the generation word holds the letter

parts.note: baby boomers were born in the population boom after 1945
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: The baby-boom generation packs outsize underwear for a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are loose knee-length knickers, a traditional item of women's underwear.

clue.text: Festival you will shortly open getting closer

indicators.note: to open the festival the words force their way into its middle

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival, such as Eid al-Fitr

indicators.note: shortly asks for the contraction to be cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: ye'll is an old form of you will

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to open a festival as it draws near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closer' looks like a comparative meaning nearer, but it is a noun: the thing that closes the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelid shuts over the eye, so it is literally the thing that closes it.

clue.text: I'm surprised, eating cereal, it sticks to the chin

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the exclamation swallows the grain

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
the oat is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise as breakfast cereal sticks to their chin.
explanation.definitionFit: A goatee is a small pointed beard grown only on the chin, like a goat's.

clue.text: Scold shedding a tear over Trump's policy, something biblical

indicators.note: shedding means losing, so the article is dropped from the crying word
in a down clue over means placed above what follows

parts.note: taken as written
Make America Great Again, Donald Trump's slogan
NT is the New Testament
the letter to be shed

explanation.surface: A critic sheds a tear over a policy that seems of biblical proportions.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, overbearing woman, a nagging shrew; scold as a noun means the same.

clue.text: I censor a depraved plot summary

indicators.note: depraved means corrupted or perverted, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A censor speaks of cutting an indecent storyline.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of a film or play's plot, a summary of the story.

clue.text: Shorebird from the pole

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long-legged wading bird
second meaning: one of a pair of poles a walker stands on

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bird migrating from the North Pole; the wader is named for legs like the walking poles.
explanation.definitionFit: The stilt is a wading bird with very long legs, and a stilt is also a supporting post or walking pole.

clue.text: Lecturer gives this pain, to secure first in Italian

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so the verb wraps around the Italian word

parts.note: to rend the heart is to pain it, tear it apart
prima is Italian for first, as in prima donna

explanation.surface: A university lecturer finds teaching Italian a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lecturer' looks like a university teacher, but here it means anyone who lectures someone about their behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lectures you is telling you off, and a telling-off is a rebuke.

clue.text: Attempted murderer maybe has a bit of respect for one old lag

indicators.note: has the bit for one says the new letter takes the place of one of the round letters

parts.note: one who poisons may be trying to kill

indicators.note: a bit of means just a single letter, the opening one, of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of respect

explanation.surface: A convict who tried to kill earns a little respect from fellow inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' means in place of one of the two Os in the poisoner. An old lag is British slang for a long-serving or repeat convict.
explanation.definitionFit: An old lag is a habitual criminal who has served many sentences, so a long-term inmate.

clue.text: Vain man from Apple for one with tidy hair

parts.note: Cox's Orange Pippin is a well-known English apple variety
to comb is to tidy the hair

explanation.surface: A vain man with neatly combed hair seems to come from Apple, the tech company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple' with its capital looks like the computer firm; it is the variety of eating apple.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is an old word for a conceited dandy, from the jester's cap shaped like a cock's crest.

clue.text: Scientist forced to lie long ago: no good coming out of that

indicators.note: forced suggests the letters are pushed and wrenched into a new order
coming out of means these letters leave the words before them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
no taken as written, plus G for good

explanation.surface: Long ago a scientist was forced to lie, and no good came of it.
explanation.walkthrough: N, O and G leave LONG to give L, and LIE plus L plus AGO is rearranged. The surface recalls the astronomer forced by the Inquisition to recant.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer and physicist who championed the Copernican view of the solar system.

clue.text: For Linnaeus, say, maggot active isn't bad

parts.note: a bot is the maggot-like larva of the botfly

indicators.note: bad means gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: A is the grammar abbreviation for active
the letters of the contraction

explanation.surface: Linnaeus, the great classifier, decides a lively maggot is not so bad after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Linnaeus was the Swedish scientist who devised the system for naming plants, an example of a plant scientist.

clue.text: Learnt about income from property

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone has learnt about making money from a property they let.
explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the sum a landlord receives for letting out a house or flat.

clue.text: For Aristotle and Euclid to appear from the start among elements of basic education is not so normal

indicators.note: among places them between the letters of the schooling basics

parts.note: the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic

indicators.note: from the start asks for just the opening letters of the two names

parts.note: the opening letter of the philosopher's name
the opening letter of the mathematician's name

explanation.surface: Greek philosophers turning up in a basic school syllabus would be unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The two initials slot into the gaps between the three Rs, one in each.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rarer is less common, so it is less ordinary or usual than another thing.

clue.text: Book Month: nothing surpasses a good book

parts.note: Oct is the calendar abbreviation for October
the AV, Authorised Version, is a translation of the Bible, the Good Book
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A literary promotion: during Book Month, nothing beats a good read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surpasses' means goes beyond, so the round letter comes after the Bible version.
explanation.definitionFit: An octavo is a book whose pages are made by folding sheets into eight leaves, a standard book size.

clue.text: New love in the far north for a number?

definitions.note: read as a noun from 'numb': something that numbs

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: in places the tennis score inside the polar word

parts.note: the Arctic is the far north of the globe
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A new romance in the Arctic inspires someone to write a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure or a song, but the question mark signals it is something that makes you numb.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, so it numbs: a numb-er.

clue.text: Its journey being through Russian city, one van avoiding periphery

definitions.text: Its journey being through Russian city

indicators.note: avoiding the periphery means skipping the outermost letters and keeping what lies inside the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters inside the phrase, ends discarded

explanation.surface: A van crosses a Russian city while keeping clear of the ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the river Neva flows through St Petersburg to the Baltic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neva is the river that runs through St Petersburg, so its course passes through a Russian city.

clue.text: Why Norwegian king can't relieve himself?

definitions.text: Why Norwegian king can't relieve himself?

parts.words: Why Norwegian king can't relieve himself?
parts.note: surface reading: a riddle about a Scandinavian monarch with no means of going to the toilet; setter's reading: the king's name splits as the letter for zero followed by a slang word for a toilet, so he has no loo

explanation.walkthrough: Several kings of Norway bore this name. Read the name as O, nothing, plus LAV, short for lavatory: no lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Olav is a royal name in Norway, borne by several monarchs including Olav V in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Turning stomachs, dirty talk

indicators.note: turning means the word for bellies is read the other way round

parts.note: tums is an informal word for stomachs

explanation.surface: Filthy talk makes the listeners' stomachs turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is obscene or indecent language or material.

clue.text: Young swimmer constantly circling lake

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the word for always surrounds the letter

parts.note: ever means always, constantly
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A young swimmer keeps doing laps round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young swimmer' sounds like a child in a pool; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, newly arrived in fresh water from the sea.

clue.text: Answer by half the people, or all of them

definitions.text: Answer by half the people, or all of them

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
men make up roughly half of people

explanation.surface: In church, the men give the response first, then the whole congregation joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the word: it is the congregation's response at the end of a prayer, said by all.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is the response said by everyone at the close of a prayer or hymn in church.
